findings.title: Forged ZIP size metadata bypasses inflated-byte memory limits
findings.what: The handler reserves and validates bytes from file.originalSize when that field exists, but observed decompressed bytes are checked and added only when originalSize is undefined. ZIP size fields are untrusted metadata, so an entry declaring a small originalSize can emit substantially more data while text continues accumulating, bypassing both maxEntryBytes and maxTotalBytes and potentially exhausting the browser tab's memory.
findings.fix: Always enforce maxEntryBytes against observedBytes and account aggregate limits from emitted chunk bytes. Treat originalSize only as an early rejection hint; do not use it as the sole accounting source or add both declared and observed sizes.
findings.acceptance: Add a test using an archive entry whose declared uncompressed size is patched below its actual emitted size; unzipBundle must reject with UploadTooLargeError once observed bytes exceed maxEntryBytes or maxTotalBytes, and a normal archive with accurate metadata must still load without double-counting.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read the cited baseline branches: lines 388-420 trust originalSize for admission/accounting, while lines 453-475 place both observed per-entry enforcement and chunk-based aggregate accounting inside `originalSize === undefined`. The existing tests only generate internally consistent ZIP metadata, so they do not invalidate the bypass.
